readall_conflicts: Among the sources already held by the project in the same check folder (from an earlier reading, not in 'works'), there is a disagreement about tone rather than stress: Haokip 2019 (Assam University PhD, ch. 3 §3.2.1 and ch. 6) gives Biate two lexical tones (H, L); Boro's Tezpur PhD ch. 1 §1.4.1 claims three tones (high, level, low, e.g. /sir/ 'report' / 'step' / 'chop'); Kharlukhi 2012 (NEHU PhD, ch. 5 §5.1) states 'Halam and Biate do not have tone'. None of these three mentions stress or accent at all (zero a full-text search for stress/accent hits in their text layers). The Foreword to the 2021 volume implies Biate too received a tone description, but the editors' summary of the Biate chapter says nothing about tone or stress.

Ch. 2 (verbal morphology) could not be downloaded (server 000).

tone.says: A single secondhand sentence in the phonological overview of a syntax thesis (p. 9): Biate 'has three types of tones, viz. high, level, and low', illustrated by a /sir/ 'report': /sir/ 'step': /sir/ 'chop' triplet whose tone diacritics did not survive in the PDF text; no measurements, no discussion of TBU, sandhi or function; presumably reflects the CFEL analysis (Brahma & Boro 2018/2021, a work listed here, still unobtained). It disagrees with Haokip 2019 (two register tones) and Kharlukhi 201…

Tezpur: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. FRONT MATTER ONLY (12 pp.: title, contents, foreword, coordinator's note, editors' introduction).
sources.note: Foreword (p. v): 'Here we now have clear phonetic descriptions, with minimal pairs, of the tone phonemes of each of these languages'. Editors' introduction (p. viii) summarizes Brahma & Boro's chapter 'A Phonological Description of Biate' (pp. 1-21) only as the phoneme inventory plus two contrastive retroflex affricates with acoustic evidence; no mention of stress. The Biate chapter itself is not online.

Chapter III Phonology (pp. 62-113) covers consonants, vowels, syllable and word structure (mono- to quadrisyllabic templates, pp. 95-103) and, under 3.2 Suprasegmental Phonology (p. 104), only tone and vowel length: 'Biate has two register tones.. high tone (H) marked by ´ and low tone (L) marked by `' (p. 105, Praat-analysed minimal pairs lói/lòi, súm/sùm, rú/rù, Table 9 p. 107); vowel length phonemic (p. 108). The strings 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence' occur nowhere in ch. III, ch. VI (6.1.2 Phonological features, pp. 298-299) or the abstract.
